name: Verification vs Validation
title: Verification vs Validation
description: Verification checks that the build matches its specification (built right); validation checks that the specification matches the real need (built the right thing). Acceptance testing is the formal demonstration that both hold.
how_it_works: Map every requirement to a verification method (test, inspection, analysis, demonstration) and separately confirm with stakeholders that the requirements themselves solve the real problem. Do both - passing verification on wrong requirements still fails the user.
key_points: Verification: does the build meet its specification?
Validation: does the specification meet the real need?
Acceptance is the formal, witnessed demonstration of both.
Skipping either one ships risk, not product.
requirements: Defined acceptance criteria with measurable pass/fail thresholds; test procedures traceable to requirements; calibrated test equipment where measurement matters.
standards: ISO 9001 quality management; ISO/IEC 25000 (SQuaRE) for software product quality; MIL-STD-810 for environmental test methods.
citations: ISO 9001:2015 quality management systems - requirements.
MIL-STD-810H environmental engineering considerations and laboratory tests.

name: Acceptance Criteria

description: Acceptance criteria are the specific, measurable conditions a build must satisfy to be accepted. Vague criteria ('works well') cannot be tested; measurable ones ('responds within 200 ms') can.

key_points: Criteria must be specific, measurable, and agreed before building.
Include numbers, tolerances, and test conditions.
Stakeholders sign the criteria, not just the final result.
Vague criteria produce arguments; measurable ones produce verdicts.
requirements: Defined acceptance criteria with measurable pass/fail thresholds; test procedures traceable to requirements; calibrated test equipment where measurement matters.

name: Burn-In and Infant Mortality
title: Burn-In and Infant Mortality
description: Burn-in operates new builds under load for a set period to force early failures before shipment. It exploits the bathtub curve: weak units fail early, and burn-in makes early happen in your factory, not the customer's hands.
how_it_works: Define burn-in duration and stress levels from failure data, monitor for failures during the run, and root-cause every burn-in failure - it is free field-failure intelligence. Ship only units that complete burn-in clean.
key_points: Burn-in forces early-life failures before shipment.
Duration and stress come from failure data, not guesswork.
Root-cause every burn-in failure - it predicts field failures.
Only clean burn-in units ship.
